$comment: Source of truth for the Cloudflare MCP portal mapping of server `tg` (mctlhq/.github#35). Every tool this server registers must appear here with an explicit decision; internal/mcp/portal_allowlist_test.go fails the build otherwise. An enabled tool must carry a `reason` that says what the tool exposes and why that is acceptable on a shared surface, and `upstream_gates`: the exact set of server-side checks the handler performs (scope tokens from requireScope/requireAnyScope, `send-gate` for evaluateSendGate/evaluateWriteGate, or `self-only` for a tool the test knows acts on the caller alone). The guard test re-derives that set from the Go source and fails on any difference, so the field cannot drift from the code. The portal allowlist is a per-server on/off switch that cannot see users; the upstream gate is the access control (decision 2026-09-12, mctlhq/.github#35). Apply with scripts/portal-allowlist-apply.sh.

tools.name: delete_messages
tools.reason: Revokes messages in the caller's own dialogs; runs through evaluateSendGate, dry run unless the full send gate is open.

tools.name: delete_telegram_account
tools.reason: Self-service hard delete of the caller's own account row on this server (not the Telegram account). Irreversible for the caller only; no other account can be named. DELIBERATE DECISION 2026-09-12 (owner, mctlhq/.github#35): exposed on the shared surface with no scope gate, so a client holding only the read scopes can drop its own session blob, and recovery needs an operator to re-run the login CLI. Accepted because the blast radius is the caller's own row and the portal cannot widen it; revisit by requiring account:manage if a client ever does this by accident.

tools.name: disconnect_telegram_account
tools.reason: Self-service: marks the caller's own session revoked and closes the MTProto client. Acts on the caller only; no admin reach. DELIBERATE DECISION 2026-09-12 (owner, mctlhq/.github#35): same as delete_telegram_account — no scope gate, irreversible without an operator-run login CLI, accepted because it reaches the caller's own session and nothing else.

tools.name: edit_message
tools.reason: Edits the caller's own sent message; runs through evaluateSendGate, so without the send scope and consent it is a dry run.

tools.name: forward_messages
tools.reason: Forwards messages between the caller's own dialogs; runs through evaluateSendGate, dry run unless the full send gate is open.

tools.name: get_media
tools.reason: Downloads media bytes of the caller's own message, only with a confirmation id from prepare_get_media; gated on telegram:messages:read and the server byte cap.

tools.name: get_messages
tools.reason: Returns message bodies from the caller's own dialogs, wrapped as untrusted content; gated upstream on the caller's telegram:messages:read scope.

tools.name: get_my_audit_log
tools.reason: Returns the caller's own audit rows with peers redacted at write time; no message bodies, no other users.

tools.name: get_my_identity
tools.reason: Returns the caller's own telegram_id, username and display name; nothing about other people or messages. It is the identity check the aggregate portal relies on.

tools.name: get_my_send_status
tools.reason: Returns booleans about the caller's own account (can_send, connected, consent); no message content, no peers. It REPORTS the send gate rather than passing one: the handler computes can_send and returns either way, so this entry claims no gate -- see reportsGateTools in internal/mcp/portal_allowlist_test.go.

tools.name: get_unread_messages
tools.reason: Returns unread message bodies of the caller's own Telegram account only; the upstream gates it on the caller's telegram:messages:read scope and there is no way to name another account.

tools.name: get_user_audit_log
tools.reason: Admin-only read of any user's audit rows (peers redacted); refused upstream without admin:users(:read).

tools.name: list_dialogs
tools.reason: Returns the caller's own dialog list (peer ids, titles, unread counts), no message bodies. Scope-gated upstream per identity.

tools.name: list_telegram_identities
tools.reason: Admin-only listing of every signed-in Telegram user with access tier and session state; the upstream refuses it with scope-denied for anyone without admin:users(:read). Only TG_LOGIN_ADMINS hold that scope.

tools.name: mint_worker_token
tools.reason: Admin-only minting of a bounded worker/Local Bridge credential; refused upstream without admin:users. The credential is returned to the admin caller only.

tools.name: pin_message
tools.reason: Pins a message in the caller's own dialog; requires the telegram:messages:pin scope, the open send gate and a confirmation id from prepare_pin_message.

tools.name: prepare_get_media
tools.reason: Issues a confirmation id for one (peer, message_id) of the caller's own account; no bytes leave; gated on telegram:messages:read.

tools.name: prepare_pin_message
tools.reason: Issues a confirmation id for a later pin_message on the caller's own dialog; performs no Telegram action by itself.

tools.name: provision_local_account
tools.reason: Admin-only creation of a fresh local-mode account; refused upstream without admin:users.

tools.name: revoke_local_bridge_device
tools.reason: Revokes a Local Bridge device of the caller's OWN account; containment action with no cross-account reach. Gated on account:manage.

tools.name: revoke_telegram_session
tools.reason: Admin-only revocation of a user's MTProto session; refused upstream without admin:users.

tools.name: revoke_worker_token
tools.reason: Admin-only revocation of a minted worker token; containment action, refused upstream without admin:users.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.reason: Full-text search over the caller's own dialogs; returns message bodies; gated upstream on telegram:messages:read.

tools.name: send_media
tools.reason: Sends a media message as the caller; same three-part send gate as send_message plus an explicit telegram:messages:send scope check.

tools.name: send_message
tools.reason: Sends a Telegram message as the caller. The upstream evaluateSendGate requires the server-wide ALLOW_SEND flag, the caller's telegram:messages:send scope (clients do not hold it) and the per-account send_enabled consent; when any is missing it dry-runs and reports why.

tools.name: set_account_mode
tools.reason: Admin-only switch of a user's account mode (hosted/local); refused upstream without admin:users.

tools.name: set_account_send
tools.reason: Admin-only flip of a user's send_enabled gate; refused upstream without admin:users.

tools.name: set_reaction
tools.reason: Sets an emoji reaction as the caller; runs through evaluateSendGate, dry run unless the full send gate is open.

tools.name: set_send_consent
tools.reason: Lets the caller grant or revoke real sending for their OWN account only; there is no telegram_id argument. Gated on the account:manage scope.

tools.name: set_telegram_access
tools.reason: Admin-only grant/revoke of the client access tier; refused upstream without admin:users.
